chunks: ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Zurʿah, from Samāʿah, who said:

I asked him about a woman who sees blood before the time of her menses. He said: “Then let her leave the salat, for sometimes the time comes early for her. Then if it continues beyond the number of her usual days in which she used to menstruate, let her wait three days after her usual days have passed. Then if she waits three days and the blood does not stop from her, let her act as the mustahadah acts.”

key_terms.الدَّمَ: the blood seen, which is being evaluated for legal classification
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: salat (prayer), which she is instructed to leave at first
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman about whom the ruling is being asked
key_terms.الْمُسْتَحَاضَةُ: a woman in a state of istiḥāḍah, whose legal rulings then apply
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ: an additional three-day waiting period after her usual days
key_terms.حَيْضِهَا: her menstruation; her normal menstrual period

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman sees bleeding before the expected time of her menses?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a woman who sees blood before her expected menstrual time. She is to leave the salat initially, then if the bleeding exceeds her normal menstrual days she waits an additional three days, and if the blood still does not stop, she follows the ruling of a mustahadah.
